## watercolor_botanical_study

> Single-specimen botanical watercolor study with latin caption, in transparent washes on visibly textured paper.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1024x1280`, aspect `4:5`
**Demo vars:** `templates/watercolor_illustration/_vars_examples/watercolor_botanical_study.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A single botanical specimen of Common Field Poppy (Latin name Papaver rhoeas) rendered as a early summer watercolor study. One stem with a few leaves, at least one fully open flower head, and one closed bud, presented as if pinned mid-page on a herbarium sheet for careful observation rather than decorative arrangement.
[2. Action] The painter has worked petal-by-petal in transparent washes, letting pigment bloom and granulate where wet meets wet, then returned with a near-dry brush to articulate veins, stem fibres, and the faint shadow under the lowest leaf. The plant sits still; the only "movement" is the migration of pigment through damp paper.
[3. Scene] Studio-flat herbarium sheet. No outdoor setting. The background is warm ivory cotton-rag paper with visible grain, a faint cold-press tooth, and one or two pale, deliberate water-tide marks left from the painter's brush rinse. No vase, no soil, no surrounding props.
[4. Composition] The specimen runs vertically, occupying roughly the central 60% of the frame; its tallest leaf reaches about 8% from the top and the lowest stem cut sits about 18% from the bottom. The latin name is set in small italic serif type 6% from the bottom edge, centered; the common-name caption runs above it as a thinner secondary line. Generous margins of bare paper on all four sides preserve the breathing room expected of a botanical plate.
[5. Style] Transparent watercolor on cotton-rag paper. Wet-into-wet petals with visible pigment blooms, dry-brush stems and leaf veins, and pale granulating shadows in the vermilion, sap green, raw umber family — soft, desaturated, never saturated digital color. Visible cold-press paper grain across the entire field. No vector edges, no flat fills, no cel-shading, no glow, no airbrush gradients.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- latin_name: "Papaver rhoeas"
- common_name: "Common Field Poppy"

Preserve (edit mode only):
- paper grain
- wet-into-wet petal blooms
- latin name italic serif

NO: vector flat color, digital airbrush gradient, photographic specimen, cel-shading anime line art, 3D render, drop shadows, cluttered background props, oversaturated neon hues
```

## watercolor_character_portrait

> Three-quarter character portrait painted in transparent watercolor washes with visible paper grain and a small footer caption.

**Artifact:** `poster`, `1024x1280`, aspect `4:5`
**Demo vars:** `templates/watercolor_illustration/_vars_examples/watercolor_character_portrait.yml`

### English

```
[1. Subject] A three-quarter-length portrait of a young apprentice cartographer, painted in transparent watercolor. The figure is shown from mid-thigh up, angled about 20 degrees off-camera, gaze drifting just past the viewer's shoulder. Mood reads as thoughtful and slightly wistful. The figure wears an oversized linen shirt with rolled sleeves as a single defining garment cue.
[2. Action] The figure stands quietly, weight on one leg, hands relaxed. There is no theatrical action; the painting earns its life from the way pigment behaves on wet paper — a soft loaded wash sliding down the cheek, a granulating shadow pooling under the jaw, a dry-brush catch at the edge of the hair. The character holds a single calm pose long enough for the wash to dry.
[3. Scene] A neutral studio-flat field of warm cotton-rag paper. No interior set, no exterior landscape, no props. A barely-there lower-frame wash of cool grey suggests "ground" without committing to a floor. Paper grain remains visible behind the figure on all sides.
[4. Composition] Vertical 4:5 frame. The head sits in the upper third, eyes near the 1/3 horizontal line; the body tapers down through the middle third and dissolves into bare paper just above the bottom edge. About 18-22% of bare paper margin frames the figure on left and right. A single small footer caption sits centered roughly 4% from the bottom edge, set in a thin serif. No frame border, no decorative flourishes.
[5. Style] Transparent watercolor on cold-press cotton-rag paper. Soft edges where wash meets wash, hard edges only where the painter chose them (collar, jawline, fingertip). Palette in the muted ochre, dusty teal, warm grey family, desaturated and atmospheric. Dry-brush hair texture, granulating pigment in the shadow side of the face. Visible paper tooth throughout; deliberate water-tide marks tolerated. No digital line art, no airbrush gradient, no cel-shading, no 3D render.

Text to render exactly (chunked into named slots):
- figure_caption: "a young apprentice cartographer"

Preserve (edit mode only):
- paper grain
- granulating shadow on face
- dry-brush hair edge
- soft watercolor edges

NO: cel-shaded anime line art, vector flat color, photographic skin, airbrush digital gradient, 3D model render, drop shadow, oversaturated neon hues, real-celebrity likeness
```
